title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Damascene — images champion; bread/wine COMMUTANTUR into body and blood
pass_a_gloss: Certainly John of Damascus himself, that Age’s Doctor most Celebrated above the rest, and concerning Orthodoxy in his four books on it glorying after the fashion of today’s claimants of Orthodoxy’s monopoly — just as he fought sharply in writing for images (the most Celebrated Chronologists Calvisius and Helvisus noting this at the years of Christ 728 and 730, pages to me 625 and 112), so he turned aside to the Pontificals’ erroneous modes of sensing and speaking about the Eucharist, or rather is to be judged to have prelude-played them, when in On the Orthodox Faith Book 4 ch. 4 he writes thus: Just as naturally bread by eating, and wine and water by drinking, are changed into the body and blood of the eater and drinker and become another body besides that prior body; So the bread and wine and water of the proposition, by the invocation and coming of the Holy Spirit, are supernaturaliter CHANGED into the body and blood of Christ — therefore to be emended by Theophylact, Whittaker noting, p. 102.
pass_b_english: John of Damascus, that age’s chief Doctor of Orthodoxy, fought sharply for images (Calvisius/Helvisus note ~728–730) — and turned toward (or rather preluded) Pontifical errors on the Eucharist.

Orthodox Faith 4.4: as bread and wine naturally change into the eater’s body, so the bread, wine, and water of the proposition are supernaturally CHANGED into Christ’s body and blood — Theophylact must emend him (Whittaker).
source_text: Certe ipse Johannes Damascenus, illius Seculi, præ ceteris, Doctor Celebratissimus, deque Orthodoxia, in suis de ea libris quatuor, ad hodiernorum, Orthodoxiæ monopolium sibi vindicantium, gloriatus modum, uti pro imaginibus scribendo decertavit acriter (annotantibus id Chronologis Celeberrimis, Calvisio & Helviso ad annum Christi 728. & 730., paginis mihi 625. & 112.) ita ad Pontificios de Eucharistia sentiendi loquendique modos erroneos divertit, seu potius hisce prælusisse censendus est, quando de fide Orthodoxa lib. 4. cap. 4. ita scribit: Quemadmodum naturaliter panis per commestionem, & vinum atque aqua, per bibitionem, in corpus & sanguinem edentis & bibentis commutantur & aliud fiunt corpus, præter prius illud corpus; Sic panis & vinum & aqua propositionis, per invocationem & adventum Sancti Spiritûs, supernaturaliter COMMUTANTUR in corpus & sanguinem Christi, à Theophylacto idcirco emendandus, notante Wittakero, pag. 102.
